title: ops-bridge-reflection-and-backlog-feb-14-2029
content:
Ops Bridge: Reflection & Future Backlog — Weekly SRE Update
Date: 2029-02-14 (notes compiled 2029-02-15)
Owner: Aisha Patel (on-call lead for week)
Attendees: Aisha Patel, Jonah Mendes, Evelyn Cho, Liam O'Neill, Maya Rivers (observability), Victor Lin (serving-runtime)

Quick summary:
- Two customer-impacting incidents this week: a GPU queue-delay spike (partial throttling, short customer-facing errors) and a metrics ingestion lag that obscured SLO burn signals for ~45 minutes. Both contained within our 4-hour escalation window, with no long-term customer data loss.
- SLO health: overall error budget usage up 3.8% vs last week; 99th P95 latency stable, but P99 shows tail increases during peak batching windows.
- Handoff: new smoothing parameter for autoscaler deployed to staging; on-call rotation updated to include explicit paging when Redis KV cache hit-rate < 60%.

Incident summaries (short):
1) GPU queue-delay spike — 2029-02-12 02:40–03:20 UTC
   - Symptom: sudden surge in request queuing on two Dedicated pools serving large-context models; queue depth rose to 4x baseline and token latency P99 increased from 420ms to 2.3s.
   - Root cause hypothesis: a combination of (a) a model rollout that increased average sequence length for a small customer cohort, and (b) suboptimal autoscaler smoothing settings that delayed additional node provisioning.
   - Mitigation: rolled back rollout to previous model variant (canary off) and manually triggered burst capacity on affected pools; autoscaler smoothing param rolled back to conservative default.
   - Action items: create gated rollout checks for sequence-length distribution (SRE + platform eng), add automatic alert when queue depth > 3x baseline for 10m, and add a runbook step to surface recent model rollouts in alerts.
   - Postmortem: initial draft posted (linked above), will run blameless review 2029-02-20.

2) Metrics ingestion lag — 2029-02-13 11:10–11:55 UTC
   - Symptom: Prometheus/remote write backlog grew after a spike in high-cardinality debugging traces; SLO dashboards showed delayed error-budget consumption leading to missed pager escalation for a 15-minute window.
   - Root cause: short-lived surge of high-cardinality tags from a debug feature in developer-experience test harness; remote-write backpressure handling delayed writes.
   - Mitigation: rate-limited the problematic debug source, cleared backlog, and temporarily increased ingestion workers.
   - Action items: add quota for high-cardinality debug metrics, add alert for ingestion backlog > 10m, deepen links between telemetry and on-call runbook.

SLO snapshot (end of week):
- API availability SLO (hosted endpoints): 99.95% monthly target — current monthly rolling: 99.92% (error budget remaining ~0.03% for month).
- Token-generation latency SLO (P95): target 650ms — weekly rolling: 612ms.
- Token-generation latency SLO (P99): target 2s — weekly rolling: 1.78s but spikes during peak batching windows up to 2.3s.
- Error budget burn: +3.8% week-over-week.

On-call handoff notes (incoming week):
- Current on-call: Aisha (primary), Jonah (secondary).
- Handoff checklist for next on-call:
  1) Review queued alerts and any silences in PagerDuty.
  2) Check cache-hit dashboards: Redis KV hit-rate, prefix cache heatmap. If hit-rate < 60% for a model-pool, page platform-eng-sma.
  3) Confirm autoscaler smoothing param (stable-default), and burst-capacity budget available for Dedicated pools.
  4) Walk through recent model rollouts in the last 48h (link to rollout dashboard in linked artifacts).
  5) Verify observability pipelines healthy (prometheus remote_write lag < 2m, alert ingestion latency < 1m).

Runbook updates (required):
- Add a new section "Model-rollout induced queue spike" with step-by-step: identify rollout -> check sequence-length distribution -> rollback variant -> trigger burst capacity -> notify platform SRE. Assigned to: Victor Lin, due 2029-02-21.
- Add an alert correlation card that surfaces recent deploys and config changes in the top section of the bridge console. Assigned to: Evelyn Cho + Maya Rivers, due 2029-02-28.

Operational experiments and observations:
- Autoscaler smoothing tweak experiment: rolled smoothing-alpha from 0.15 to 0.35 in staging for 6 hours; observed fewer oscillations but slower scale-up on sudden spikes. Decision: adopt a hybrid policy (conservative smoothing for baseline, aggressive emergency-burst trigger). Jonah to draft proposal (SRE-4021).
- Prefix/KV cache telemetry: discovered underinstrumented evictions for one busy model pool. Added eviction-rate metric and heatmap; will evaluate next week.

Backlog and near-term priorities (ranked):
1) Gated rollout checks for sequence-length distribution (high priority, cross-team).
2) Automated alert for queue depth > 3x baseline for 10m (high).
3) Add ingestion-backlog alert and quota for high-cardinality debug metrics (medium).
4) Runbook authoring: "Model-rollout induced queue spike" + alert correlation card (medium).
5) Autoscaler hybrid policy RFC and canary in prod (low→medium).
6) Observability: eviction heatmap dashboard and weekly report (low).

Risks/open questions:
- We currently allow experimental debug metrics to be emitted with few soft quotas; this will continue to risk telemetry reliability unless we gate it.
- Blast radius for model rollout checks — how many customers should block a rollout? Proposal: if top-10 customers show >25% increase in median sequence length, gate rollout. Feedback requested from product/eng.

Community notes / communications:
- CS: notified of GPU queue incident; account-level remediation notes prepared for affected customers.
- Product: asked to consider releasing a canary flag for sequence-length sampling in rollout tooling.

Meeting & follow-ups this week:
- 2029-02-16 15:00 UTC — Postmortem dry-run (blameless) — required: Aisha, Victor, Jonah, product rollout lead.
- 2029-02-18 10:00 UTC — Observability sync: eviction heatmap + ingestion resilience.
- Jonah to own SRE-4021 autoscaler RFC draft by 2029-02-20.

Notes to next on-call: focus initially on queue-depth and ingestion backlog dashboards; if you see queue depth trending up, prioritize surfacing recent rollouts and enabling burst capacity quickly. Pager escalation threshold temporarily lowered for this week: queue-depth > 2.5x baseline for 8m.

End of update.
(Prepared as a working doc — please add comments inline; want to finalize postmortem and runbook edits before next rotation.)
